brief: Fed credibility on the long end and a pullback in spot oil have taken pressure off Treasury yields. The curve has flattened and front-end stubbornness is driving a forced unwind in positioning. The market narrative has shifted from pricing 2 rate cuts to pricing 3 hikes, with one delivered and two more still to be timed, and the note asks whether $80 oil is a hidden tailwind that makes those hikes unnecessary. Positioning is now much cleaner heading into month-end. On AI, Meta's Muse-driven 43% one-month rally sits against Oracle's force majeure decision, which reopened AI credit questions and pushed investors to re-underwrite contracted obligations against expected capex benefits. $18bn of debt tied to Oracle's Jupiter data center was reportedly quoted at 89-91 cents. Sell-side depreciation forecasts ($255bn in 2026 vs $768bn capex, and $581bn in 2029 vs $1.2tn capex) raise the same ROI question. Separately, the note traces an accelerating venture cycle: OpenAI reached $10bn-to-$100bn revenue in about 3 years versus 6-10 years for Meta, Amazon, Nvidia, Google and Tesla, alongside the largest VC exit in history.
